category_title: Students with physical disabilities who struggle with initial self-evaluation and volume of speech
minimal_context: The student is working on the 'Go for Goal!' self-evaluation report in a group setting during a Chinese lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please fill out your 'Go for Goal!' self-evaluation report with your group. What are your strengths?

STUDENT: Love to do craft. When I encounter difficulties, I become brave. When I get the tasks from the teachers, I will be responsible for finishing them on time.

TUTOR: What are your goals for this term?

STUDENT: (Speaking very quietly) I have to speak a bit louder, and try to ask people’s help to take notes. I need to learn to speak slowly.

TUTOR: Your group members are giving you advice on your goals right now. Please write down their comments.

STUDENT: (Speaking too quickly and quietly, while struggling to take notes independently) My weakness is I do not like to listen to people’s advice.

options.A: Allow the student to keep the report under the condition she does not show her group, and break for lunch.
options.B: Issue the sanction of a verbal warning to the student during the group evaluation activity.
options.C: Ignore the student's behavior (where safe to do so) during the group evaluation activity.
options.D: Ask the student to think of one more thing to improve if the initial goal is not enough.
